introduction: On this Sunday, Joshua asks the people to choose whom they will serve, and they answer that they will serve the Lord. In the Gospel, many disciples find Jesus' teaching on the bread of life too hard and walk away. Jesus asks the Twelve whether they will go too, and Peter answers: Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life. Let us renew our choice to follow him.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord has the words of eternal life. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may remain faithful to the teaching of Christ, even when it is hard to accept. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have walked away from the faith: that Christ may call them back, and that we may welcome them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For married couples: that they may love each other as Christ loves the Church and gave himself up for her. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who face a hard decision: that, like Joshua, they may choose to serve the Lord. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may answer with Peter: Lord, to whom would we go?. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you have given us your Son, who has the words of eternal life. Keep us faithful to him, and help our homes to serve you. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: To whom would we go?
reflection.body:
At the end of his life, Joshua gathers all the tribes of Israel and puts a choice before them: "choose today whom you will serve." He makes his own decision clear: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD." The people remember all that God has done for them, and they answer, "Therefore we also will serve the LORD; for he is our God."

The Gospel brings us to the end of Jesus' teaching on the bread of life. He has told the crowd that he will give his flesh to eat, and many of his own disciples find it too much: "This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?" Jesus does not soften his words. John records a sad moment: "At this, many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him."

Then Jesus turns to the Twelve: "You don't also want to go away, do you?" Peter answers for them all: "Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life." Peter does not claim to understand everything. But he knows where life is found.

Faith sometimes asks us to accept what we cannot fully grasp, and to stay with Jesus when others leave. The Eucharist is one such mystery: real bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ.

Paul speaks about Christian marriage in the light of Christ's love. He begins with mutual respect, "subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Christ," and he gives husbands a demanding model: "love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her."

Every Christian life includes moments of choice like Joshua's and Peter's. This week, renew your own choice in prayer, in your own words: Lord, I choose you. And pray for someone you know who has walked away.
